High fees, low customer service

I entrusted my dog ​​to this establishment, and the experience left a bad taste in my mouth. The problem isn't so much the base price as the sheer number of extras: fees are added here, fees there, and you end up paying nearly $200 for barely 24 hours of boarding.

A few examples: Medication is charged at $8 per pill—a dog taking three pills a day costs almost $25 just for that, on top of the boarding fee. Then there's a $25 package of three walks, but be warned: the three walks must be completed on the same day, otherwise they're forfeited. All this while group outings are supposed to be included.

These rules make no sense and seem designed primarily to inflate the bill. The owner makes no effort to explain, accommodate, or retain her customers.

I do not recommend it.

I’ve used MUZO for boarding my dog several times in the past, and I didn’t really have any issues. The last time I used them, it was a different story.   When I picked up Lola at 2:30 pm, they brought her out and when she came to me, she was so desperate to go outside to do her business.  She was always so excited to see me, but that time was different, she just wanted to run outside.  Muzo informed me that they take the dogs out 3 times a day; morning,  midday and evening.  I am very sceptical of that, since Lola would not have been that desperate to go outside midday.  Very disappointed.   For the price you pay,  there is much better out there. Do not recommend.

Very good  service

Not sure if I would use them again. I asked for updates via any method they preferred during my cat’s two week stay, but I didn’t receive anything. I even called to ask a second time and was assured they would send me a photo of her, but still received nothing.

Was also told that they’d have to downgrade her suite during the last few days of her stay, yet charged me for the large suite the whole duration. I believe they moved her to a smaller suite and just didn’t want to refund the difference.
